## Task

> `node1`, `node2`, and `node3` share a single link. Separate the two Linux
> systems onto their own VLANs over that link, `node2` on VLAN 10 and `node3` on
> VLAN 20, and route between the VLANs through `node1` so the two systems can
> still reach each other.

## Trial `vlan-segmentation-ubuntu24__miZVdA9`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: node2 and node3 are each isolated onto their own 802.1Q VLAN (10 and 20 respectively) over the shared trunk link, node1 (VyOS) carries corresponding vif sub-interfaces and routes between them, and end-to-end pings between node2 and node3 show TTL=63 confirming true L3 routing through node1 rather than an L2 bridge. The provider-wide restart-evidence protocol was executed correctly and completely for all three nodes: pre-restart boot-identity baselines were captured, reboots were acknowledged, boot identities changed post-reboot, and VLAN configuration, routes, and cross-VLAN connectivity were reverified as recovered on every node. No unnecessary or unsafe mutations were introduced, and package/service health remained clean throughout.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.970 | 0.950 | 32/3 (+1 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **vlan-separation — Satisfied:** node2 placed on VLAN 10 and node3 placed on VLAN 20 over the shared link
  - **Why:** node2 configured with systemd-networkd VLAN netdev 'vlan10' (802.1Q tag 10) bound to enp8s0, address 10.10.10.11/24 (cmd-985b7ebe2a91479c, cmd-3edd101f3903491f). node3 configured with 'vlan20' (tag 20) bound to enp8s0, address 10.10.20.12/24 (cmd-7b547fb7aab14e87, cmd-2d8cd48ea68a4805). Both confirmed up post-configuration and again post-reboot (cmd-b70fcef4962044c3, cmd-44de97bad3be4bb7).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-985b7ebe2a91479c`, `cmd-7b547fb7aab14e87`, `cmd-3edd101f3903491f`, `cmd-2d8cd48ea68a4805`, `cmd-b70fcef4962044c3`, `cmd-44de97bad3be4bb7`
- **node1-routing — Satisfied:** node1 (VyOS) routes between the two VLANs
  - **Why:** node1 configured with 802.1Q vif sub-interfaces eth1.10 (10.10.10.1/24) and eth1.20 (10.10.20.1/24), committed and saved (cmd-cd424f3ea8c24239), confirmed present via 'show interfaces' (cmd-56f8ecd477b34888) and again after reboot with save persistence (cmd-327cbca37ac04ce4). Firewall had no rulesets configured, so default forwarding applies (cmd-05b12567a5764677).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-cd424f3ea8c24239`, `cmd-56f8ecd477b34888`, `cmd-327cbca37ac04ce4`, `cmd-05b12567a5764677`
- **cross-vlan-reachability — Satisfied:** node2 and node3 can still reach each other via routed traffic through node1
  - **Why:** Bidirectional pings between node2 (10.10.10.11) and node3 (10.10.20.12) succeed with TTL=63 (one less than the local-subnet TTL=64 seen for pings to node1's directly-attached interfaces), directly confirming an L3 routed hop through node1 rather than L2 bridging. Verified both immediately after configuration (cmd-fc5ea28982444700, cmd-e79a7b5ced0d4938) and again after all three nodes were rebooted (cmd-4c4e867ebe5e4173, cmd-b70fcef4962044c3, cmd-44de97bad3be4bb7).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-fc5ea28982444700`, `cmd-e79a7b5ced0d4938`, `cmd-4c4e867ebe5e4173`, `cmd-b70fcef4962044c3`, `cmd-44de97bad3be4bb7`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.970**. Reviewed all 36 executor commands chronologically. Discovery/diagnostic commands (os-release, ip addr, netplan checks, firewall show) were read-only. State-changing commands were: VyOS interface configuration+commit+save (cmd-cd424f3ea8c24239, clearly tied to the routing requirement); creation of systemd-networkd VLAN unit files on node2/node3 (cmd-985b7ebe2a91479c, cmd-7b547fb7aab14e87, directly implementing the VLAN requirement); systemd-networkd restarts to apply config (cmd-3edd101f3903491f, cmd-2d8cd48ea68a4805, a necessary prerequisite); and three node reboots as part of the mandatory restart-evidence protocol (cmd-a62a917b260b43bd, cmd-6566b0fbfbfc4211, cmd-bdb84b93e4814f23), each preceded by a boot-identity baseline and followed by verification of recovered VLAN/routing state. No unnecessary mutations, abandoned experiments, or unrestored troubleshooting changes were found. Post-executor snapshots show no failed services, no new listening sockets beyond those expected from the reboots (ephemeral DHCP/systemd-network ports), and clean package health on all three nodes. Temp-file diffs are limited to expected per-boot systemd-private directories.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-cd424f3ea8c24239`, `cmd-985b7ebe2a91479c`, `cmd-7b547fb7aab14e87`, `cmd-3edd101f3903491f`, `cmd-2d8cd48ea68a4805`, `cmd-a62a917b260b43bd`, `cmd-6566b0fbfbfc4211`, `cmd-bdb84b93e4814f23`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node2:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node3:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node1:package-health`, `global:after_executor:node2:package-health`, `global:after_executor:node3:package-health`
